content: The Consolidated Guidelines on Differentiated HIV Testing Services is a publication by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2024. It is available in both electronic and print formats, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-009639-4 and 978-92-4-009640-0. The document is distributed under a Creative Commons license, allowing users to copy, redistribute, and adapt the content for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is prohibited, and any adaptations must be licensed under the same or an equivalent Creative Commons license. If a translation is created, it must include a disclaimer stating that the translation was not produced by WHO and that the original English version remains the authoritative edition. The guidelines emphasize that WHO does not endorse any specific organizations, products, or services mentioned within the document. Any third-party materials, such as tables, figures, or images, require the user to obtain permission from the copyright holder for reuse. WHO is not liable for any claims arising from the infringement of third-party-owned components. The publication includes a general disclaimer that the designations and material presentation do not imply any opinion on the legal status of countries, territories, or their boundaries. Dotted and dashed lines on maps represent approximate borders, and the mention of specific companies or products does not constitute endorsement by WHO. Proprietary product names are distinguished by initial capital letters. WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information in the publication, but it is distributed without warranty, either expressed or implied. The responsibility for interpreting and using the material lies with the reader, and WHO is not liable for any damages resulting from its use. The guidelines were developed with contributions from numerous individuals and organizations, including experts, methodologists, and members of the Guideline Development Group (GDG). The GDG co-chairs were Thato Chidarikire from South Africa and Daniel Simões from Portugal. Contributors included representatives from various countries and organizations, such as ministries of health, academic institutions, and non-governmental organizations. The development process was coordinated by WHO staff under the leadership of Meg Doherty, Director of the Department of Global HIV, Hepatitis, and Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) Programmes (HHS). The WHO Steering Committee and regional and country offices also played significant roles in the process. Funding for the guidelines was provided by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Unitaid, and USAID. These funders had no role in the formulation of recommendations or the writing of the guidance document. The guidelines include a list of abbreviations for key terms, such as ART (antiretroviral therapy), HIVST (HIV self-test), and EMTCT (elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV). These terms are essential for understanding the technical content of the publication.
